23. Recognition principles and measuring methods of 
revenue
The Group’s operating revenue primarily comprises 
revenue from the sale of goods and revenue from 
the provision of services.
The Group recognizes revenue upon fulfilment of its 
contractual obligations, that is, when the customer 
obtains control of the relevant goods or services.
Where a contract comprises two or more 
performance obligations, the Group, at the inception 
of the contract, allocates the transaction price to 
each individual performance obligation in proportion 
to the relative selling prices of the goods or services 
promised under each individual performance 
obligation, and measures revenue based on the 
transaction price allocated to each individual 
performance obligation.
The transaction price is the amount of consideration 
to which the Group expects to be entitled in 
exchange for the transfer of goods or services to a 
customer, excluding amounts collected on behalf 
of third parties. The transaction price recognized 
by the Group does not exceed the amount up to 
which the cumulative revenue recognized is highly 
probable not to be subject to a material reversal 
when the related uncertainty is resolved. Amounts 
expected to be refunded to customers are not 
included in the transaction price and are treated as 
liabilities. Where a contract contains a significant 
financing component, the Group determines the 
transaction price as the amount that the customer 
would be required to pay in cash if the customer 
were to obtain control of the goods or services. The 
difference between this transaction price and the 
contract consideration is amortized over the term 
of the contract using the effective interest method. 
At the commencement of the contract, the Group 
disregards any significant financing component in 
the contract if it expects the interval between the 
customer obtaining control of the goods or services 
and the customer’s payment of the consideration to 
be no more than one year.

amount thereof. As to taxable income with 
deductible loss and tax deduction that can be 
deducted in the future as specified by tax laws, 
corresponding deferred income tax assets shall be 
recognized. For temporary difference from initial 
recognition of goodwill, corresponding deferred 
income tax liabilities will not be recognized. For 
the temporary difference from initial recognition of 
assets or liabilities incurred in transaction which 
is not business combination and the occurrence 
of which has no impact on the accounting profits 
and the taxable income (or deductible losses), 
corresponding deferred income tax assets and 
deferred income tax liabilities will not be recognized.

tax liabilities shall be measured at applicable tax 
rate during the anticipated period for recovering 
such assets or paying off such liabilities on the 
balance sheet date.
The Group recognizes deferred income tax assets 
arising from deductible temporary differences to the 
extent that it is probable that taxable income will be 
available against which the deductible temporary 
differences can be utilized.

27. Fair values measurement
On each balance sheet date, the Group measures 
investment property, derivative financial instruments 
and equity instrument investments at fair value. 
Fair value is the price that a market participant 
would receive to sell an asset, or would pay to 
transfer a liability, in an orderly transaction at the 
measurement date.
Assets and liabilities measured or disclosed at 
fair value in the financial statements are classified 
into fair value hierarchies based on the lowest 
level of inputs that is significant to the fair value 
measurement as a whole: Level 1 inputs, which 
are unadjusted quoted prices in active markets 
for identical assets or liabilities available at the 
measurement date; Level 2 inputs, which are 
directly or indirectly observable inputs for the 
relevant asset or liability, other than Level 1 inputs; 
Level 3 inputs, which are unobservable inputs for 
the relevant asset or liability.

III. SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES AND 
ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES (continued)
27. Fair values measurement (continued)
On each balance sheet date, the Group reassesses 
the assets and liabilities recognized in the financial 
statements that are measured at fair value on 
a continuous basis to determine whether there 
has been a reclassification between fair value 
measurement hierarchy.
For financial instruments traded on active markets, 
the Group determines their fair value based on 
quoted prices in those active markets; for financial 
instruments not traded on active markets, the 
Group determines their fair value using valuation 
techniques, primarily the discounted cash 
flow model. The key inputs for these valuation 
techniques include: for debt instruments, the risk￾free rate, credit spread and liquidity premium; and 
for equity instruments, valuation multiples and 
liquidity discount.
Fair values in Level 3 are determined on the basis of 
the Group’s valuation models, such as discounted 
cash flow model. The Group also takes into account 
the initial transaction price, recent transactions 
in the same or similar financial instruments, or 
third-party transactions in comparable financial 
instruments. As at 30 June 2026, Level 3 financial 
assets measured at fair value utilized significant 
unobservable inputs, such as discount rates, in 
their valuation; however, their fair value was not 
significantly sensitive to reasonable changes in 
these significant unobservable inputs.

七、 與金融工具相關風險
本集團在日常活動中面臨各種金融
工具風險，主要包括市場風險、信
用風險及流動性風險等。與這些金
融工具有關的風險，以及本集團為
降低這些風險所採取的風險管理政
策如下所述。本集團管理層對這些
風險敞口進行管理和監控以確保將
上述風險控制在限定的範圍之內。
1. 各類風險管理目標和政策
本集團從事風險管理的目標
是在風險和收益之間取得適
當的平衡，將風險對本集團
經營業績的負面影響降低到
最低水平，使股東及其它權
益投資者的利益最大化。基
於該風險管理目標，本集團
風險管理的基本策略是確定
和分析本集團所面臨的各種
風險，建立適當的風險承受
底線並進行風險管理，並及
時可靠地對各種風險進行監
督，將風險控制在限定的範
圍之內。

INSTRUMENTS
In the course of its daily operation, the Group is exposed 
to various risks associated with financial instruments, 
primarily including market risk, credit risk and liquidity risk. 
The risks associated with these financial instruments, and 
the Group’s risk management policies adopted to mitigate 
such risks, are set out below. The Group’s management 
manages and monitors these exposures to ensure that the 
aforementioned risks are kept within a prescribed scope.
1. Objective and policies of various risks 
management
The Group engages in risk management with the 
aim of achieving an appropriate balance between 
risk and return, where the negative effects of 
risks against the operating results of the Group 
are minimized, and to maximize the interest of 
Shareholders and other stakeholders. Based on 
such risk management objectives, the fundamental 
strategy of risk management of the Group is to 
ascertain and analyze all types of risk exposures 
of the Group, establish appropriate risk tolerance 
thresholds, carry out risk management procedures 
and perform risk monitoring on all kinds of risks in 
a timely and reliable manner, thus containing risk 
exposures within a prescribed scope.

period exceeds 90 days”. However,

to the internal or external information, 
before any credit enhancement is

amount may not be recovered in 
full, the Group may also deem it as 
the credit impairment. The credit 
impairment of financial assets may 
be caused by the common effects 
of multiple incidents, and it is not 
necessarily caused by any incident 
which can be identified alone.

1

contents of this announcement.
CHINA ISOTOPE & RADIATION CORPORATION
中國同輻股份有限公司
(A joint stock company incorporated in the People’s Republic of China with limited liability)
(Stock Code: 1763)
CONNECTED TRANSACTIONS AND DISCLOSEABLE TRANSACTIONS
CNNC (ZHEJIANG) NUCLEAR TECHNOLOGY APPLICATION 
INDUSTRIAL INVESTMENT FUND PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT
PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT
On 28 August 2026, the Board of the Company has approved the Company’s entering into of the 
Partnership Agreement with CNNC, CNNC Capital, CNNC Fund, National Industrial Investment 
Fund, Zhejiang Province Entrepreneurship Risk Investment Guide Fund, Jiaxing Changchuang 
Industrial Investment, and Haiyan County State-owned Assets Investment.
IMPLICATIONS OF THE LISTING RULES
As at the date of this announcement, CNNC directly and indirectly holds approximately 73.83% 
of the Company’s total issued share capital through CIAE, NPIC, CNNC Fund and CNNC 404, 
and is the controlling Shareholder and a connected person of the Company. CNNC Capital and 
CNNC Fund are wholly-owned subsidiaries of CNNC. Therefore, CNNC Capital and CNNC 
Fund are associates of CNNC and constitute connected persons of the Company under Chapter 
14A of the Listing Rules. Accordingly, the entering into of the Partnership Agreement and the 
transactions contemplated thereunder constitute connected transactions of the Company.
As one or more of the applicable percentage ratios of the transactions under the Partnership 
Agreement exceed 5% but are less than 25%, the transactions contemplated thereunder are 
subject to the reporting, announcement, annual review and independent shareholders’ approval 
requirements under Chapter 14A of the Listing Rules. The entering into of the Partnership 
Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereunder also constitute discloseable transactions 
of the Company.

[PDF PAGE 2]
2
EXTRAORDINARY GENERAL MEETING
The Company will convene an extraordinary general meeting for the Independent Shareholders 
to consider and approve, by way of ordinary resolution, the Partnership Agreement and the 
transactions contemplated thereunder. The Independent Board Committee of the Company 
will advise the Independent Shareholders on the Partnership Agreement and the transactions 
contemplated thereunder, and has appointed Rainbow Capital as the independent financial 
adviser to advise the Independent Board Committee and the Independent Shareholders on the 
Partnership Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereunder.
A circular, containing details of the Partnership Agreement and the transactions contemplated 
thereunder, the letter from the Independent Board Committee and advice from Rainbow 
Capital, will be despatched to the Shareholders within 15 working days after the date of this 
announcement.
The Directors (excluding the independent non-executive Directors, whose opinions will be 
formed after taking into account the advice of the independent financial adviser) consider that 
the terms of the Partnership Agreement have been determined after arm’s length negotiations 
on normal commercial terms, and that the transactions contemplated thereunder are fair and 
reasonable, will be entered into in the ordinary and usual course of business of the Group, and 
are in the interests of the Company and the Shareholders as a whole.
I. INTRODUCTION
On 28 August 2026, the Board approved the Company’s entering into of the Partnership 
Agreement with CNNC, CNNC Capital, CNNC Fund, National Industrial Investment Fund, 
Zhejiang Province Entrepreneurship Risk Investment Guide Fund, Jiaxing Changchuang 
Industrial Investment, and Haiyan County State-owned Assets Investment.
II. MAJOR TERMS OF THE PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT
Parties: CNNC Fund (as the general partner)
The Company (as the limited partner)
CNNC (as the limited partner)
CNNC Capital (as the limited partner)
National Industrial Investment Fund (as the limited partner)
Zhejiang Province Entrepreneurship Risk Investment Guide Fund (as 
the limited partner)
Jiaxing Changchuang Industrial Investment (as the limited partner)
Haiyan County State-owned Assets Investment (as the limited 
partner)

[PDF PAGE 3]
3
Name of partnership: CNNC (Zhejiang) Nuclear Technology Application Industrial 
Investment Fund Partnership (Limited Partnership)
Place of registration: Jiaxing City, Zhejiang Province
Amount of 
 contribution:
The total capital contributions proposed to be committed by the 
partners are RMB3,000 million, of which CNNC Fund proposes to 
commit RMB30 million (representing 1%), the Company proposes 
to commit RMB400 million (representing 13.33%), National 
Industrial Investment Fund proposes to commit RMB1,000 million 
(representing 33.33%), CNNC proposes to commit RMB200 million 
(representing 6.67%), CNNC Capital proposes to commit RMB170 
million (representing 5.67%), Zhejiang Province Entrepreneurship 
Risk Investment Guide Fund proposes to commit RMB400 million 
(representing 13.33%), Jiaxing Changchuang Industrial Investment 
proposes to commit RMB400 million (representing 13.33%), and 
Haiyan County State-owned Assets Investment proposes to commit 
RMB400 million (representing 13.33%). The contribution to the 
Fund was determined by the Parties after arm’s length negotiations 
with reference to the capital requirements of the Fund. The Company 
intends to finance its capital contribution from the internal resources 
of the Group. The Company will not consolidate its financial 
statements with those of the Fund.
Method of 
 contribution:
All partners shall make contributions to the Fund in RMB in cash in 
accordance with the notice of payment of contribution given by the 
executive partner to the limited partners. The date of receipt of funds 
specified in the notice of payment of the first contribution is the first 
closing date.
All partners shall pay their subscribed capital contributions in full in 
two instalments during the investment period, with 40% and 60% of 
their respective subscribed capital contributions payable in the first 
and second instalments, respectively.
Liabilities of the 
 partners for the 
 debts of the Fund:
The general partner assumes unlimited joint and several liability for 
the debts of the Fund, and the limited partners are responsible for the 
debts of the Fund to the extent of the amount of capital contribution 
committed by them.
Purpose and scope 
 of investment:
Engaging in investment activities, primarily through the acquisition, 
holding and disposal of interests in investment portfolios, to generate 
investment returns for the partners.
The Fund will invest in the application areas of nuclear technology, 
including the production and preparation of isotope, nuclear medical 
equipment and innovative pharmaceuticals, industrial irradiation 
and inspection, security inspection and protection, as well as related 
applications and key upstream and downstream segments of nuclear 
technology in the industrial, agricultural, medical, environmental 
protection and security fields.

[PDF PAGE 4]
4
Investment strategy 
 and target sectors
100% of the Fund’s investments shall be made in the nuclear 
technology application sector, including the production and 
preparation of isotopes, nuclear medical equipment and innovative 
pharmaceuticals, industrial irradiation and inspection, security 
screening and protection, as well as relevant applications of nuclear 
technology in the industrial, agricultural, medical, environmental 
protection and safety sectors, together with key upstream and 
downstream links.
Specifically, the Fund intends to focus primarily on the following 
three investment tracks:
The Fund’s investment strategy is to identify and invest in 
enterprises and projects in the foregoing fields with technological 
competitiveness, commercialisation potential and growth prospects 
so as to generate investment returns.
Investment track Principal investment focus
Isotope production and 
 preparation
Isotope production reactors, accelerator￾based isotope production, isotope 
extraction from spent fuel and large￾scale production of stable isotopes, with 
a focus on securing scarce upstream 
production capacity and strengthening 
domestic isotope supply
Nuclear medical and 
 high-end equipment
Innovative radiopharmaceuticals, large￾scale nuclear medical equipment, high￾end irradiation equipment, security 
inspection equipment and radiation 
monitoring equipment, with a focus 
on technological innovation, domestic 
substitution and commercialization
Key components and 
 upstream materials
Key components, critical upstream 
materials and other technologies relevant 
to nuclear technology applications and 
emerging industries, with a focus on 
addressing technological bottlenecks 
and capturing valuation upside from 
technological breakthroughs
Investment targets 
 selection criteria
The Fund intends to invest principally in mature-stage and growth￾stage projects, while allocating a relatively smaller portion of its 
capital to seed-stage projects.

[PDF PAGE 5]
5
For mature-stage projects, the Fund will generally prioritise 
established nuclear technology application enterprises with validated 
business models, stable management and technical teams, established 
customer bases and revenue streams, positive or near-positive cash 
flow, competitive positions in their respective market segments and 
identifiable exit prospects, including the potential for an IPO or 
industrial acquisition within approximately three to five years.
For growth-stage projects, the Fund will primarily focus on sectors 
with relatively clear growth prospects, including innovative 
radiopharmaceuticals, nuclear medical equipment and irradiation 
applications. Target companies would generally be expected to 
have products that have reached the clinical, pilot production or 
more advanced stages, or have otherwise achieved commercial 
validation; possess proprietary intellectual property or identifiable 
technological barriers; have management teams with both research 
and development capability and commercial experience; demonstrate 
a clear path to profitability; and possess differentiated competitive 
advantages and the potential to become leading participants in their 
respective market segments.
For seed-stage projects, the Fund will selectively invest in 
commercialisable technological achievements originating from 
national research institutes and research institutes affiliated 
with central state-owned enterprises, particularly technologies 
which may address strategically important technological 
bottlenecks in the nuclear technology application industry. Such 
investments are intended to provide long-term capital support 
for the commercialisation of original and potentially disruptive 
technologies.
Deployment plan The Fund has an investment period of four years from the first 
closing date. The partners are expected to contribute their respective 
capital commitments in two instalments of 40% and 60%. Other 
than the first instalment, CNNC Fund may generally initiate the 
subsequent capital call only after 80% of the preceding contribution 
has been utilised or reserved for investments approved by the 
investment committee, Fund expenses or other permitted purposes. 
Accordingly, capital will be deployed progressively by reference to 
the actual progress of suitable investments.
During the investment period, the Fund is expected to deploy 
capital substantially in accordance with the three-track allocation 
and to maintain a diversified portfolio across different stages of 
development, with mature-stage and growth-stage investments 
forming the principal part of the portfolio and seed-stage projects 
accounting for a relatively limited portion.

[PDF PAGE 6]
6
Business scope: Engaging in activities including equity investment, investment 
management and asset management through private equity funds 
(business activities can only be conducted after completing 
registration and filing with the Asset Management Association of 
China) (except for projects subject to approval according to law, 
business activities shall be carried out independently according 
to the business license) (subject to the business scope as finally 
approved by the company registration authority).
Term of operation: Long-term, starting from the date of issuance of the first business 
licence of the Fund.
Valid duration,
 investment period, 
 exit period and 
 extension period:
The “valid duration” is eight (8) years from the first closing day;
The “investment period” is four (4) years from the first closing day;
The “exit period” commences on the day after the expiry of the 
investment period and ends on the expiry date of the valid duration;
Subject to the operational needs of the Fund, the valid duration 
may be extended with the consent of partners holding more than 
two-thirds of the partnership interests of all partners (including the 
National Industrial Investment Fund). The partnership may extend 
the valid duration up to two times, with each extension not exceeding 
one year (the extension period may apply to the investment period 
and the exit period).
Implementation of 
 partnership affairs:
The general partner acts as executive partner to implement 
partnership affairs.

[PDF PAGE 7]
7
Management fees: As consideration for the daily operation and investment management 
services provided by the fund manager to the Fund, all parties have 
agreed that the management fees shall be paid by the Fund to CNNC 
Fund in accordance with the following arrangements:
(1) During the investment period (including any extension of the 
investment period), the annual management fee shall be 1.8% 
of the total paid-in capital contribution amount;
(2) From the day after the expiry of the investment period to the 
expiry date of the valid duration (excluding any extension of 
the exit period), the annual management fee shall be 1.5% of 
the total investment principal amount of projects that have not 
yet been exited;
(3) No management fee shall be charged during any extension of 
the exit period or during the liquidation period.
Distribution: (I) Cash distribution
1. Distribution of cash income received from investment 
projects shall be carried out according to the following 
order:
(1) Return of capital contribution to each partner.
(2) If a remaining balance exists, the amount will be 
distributed as hurdle return to each partner (simple 
interest at 8%).
(3) The excess profit will be shared on a pro rata 
basis. If a remaining balance exists, 20% will be 
distributed to the general partner; 80% will be 
distributed to each limited partner in accordance 
with the relative ratio of the paid-in capital 
contribution amount by each limited partner.
2. Timing for distribution of cash income:
In principle, no later than 90 days after the Fund receives 
the relevant proceeds.

[PDF PAGE 8]
8
3. Upon expiry or termination and liquidation of the 
Fund, all investment projects shall be calculated on an 
aggregate basis, and a final consolidated calculation shall 
be conducted in accordance with the above distribution 
principles. If the excess profit actually paid to the general 
partner exceeds the amount of excess profit it is entitled 
to receive as calculated based on the above distribution 
principles after aggregating all investment projects, the 
general partner shall return the excess amount to the 
Fund, or such excess amount shall be deducted from the 
liquidation distribution amount payable to the general 
partner, and shall be distributed among the partners 
entitled to receive such distributions in accordance with 
the above distribution principles. Notwithstanding the 
foregoing, the general partner’s aggregate clawback 
obligation shall in no event exceed the amount of excess 
profit actually received by the general partner, net of any 
taxes paid or payable thereon.
(II) Non-cash distribution
Before completion of the liquidation of the partnership, the 
executive partner shall make its reasonable endeavours to 
realize the investments of the partnership and avoid making 
non-cash distribution. However, if the investments cannot be 
realised or if, in the opinion of the executive partner, non-cash 
distribution would better serve the interests of all partners, such 
distribution shall be made in non-cash form upon unanimous 
consent of all partners.
Except for assets with a readily ascertainable market price, 
the value of all assets distributed in non-cash form pursuant 
to the above arrangements shall be determined by reference 
to the valuation prepared by a professional valuer being an 
Independent Third Party, designated by the executive partner.
The proportion, method and other arrangements for non-cash 
distributions shall be governed by the provisions applicable to 
cash distributions.

[PDF PAGE 9]
9
Management and 
 decision-making:
CNNC Fund, as the executive partner and fund manager, is 
responsible for the daily operation and investment management of 
the Fund.
The Investment Committee shall be established under the Fund to 
consider and decide on investment matters relating to investment 
projects, material post-investment management matters and exit 
matters.
The Investment Committee shall comprise five (5) members. The 
National Industrial Investment Fund shall be entitled to appoint 
one (1) member, while the remaining four (4) members shall be 
nominated by CNNC and its affiliated enterprises.
Each member of the Investment Committee shall have one vote. 
Resolutions of the Investment Committee shall be passed only upon 
the affirmative votes of no less than four-fifths (4/5) of all members 
of the Investment Committee.
If the Fund’s aggregate committed capital contributions to a single 
investment portfolio exceed 20% of the total capital contributions 
committed to the Fund, the unanimous consent of the meeting of the 
Partners shall be required.
Following the Fund’s investment, the executive partner shall conduct 
ongoing monitoring on the relevant investment portfolio.
Investment 
 Committee 
 observers:
The Company, the National Industrial Investment Fund, Zhejiang 
Province Entrepreneurship Risk Investment Guide Fund and Jiaxing 
Changchuang Industrial Investment shall each be entitled to appoint 
one observer. Observers may attend meetings of the Investment 
Committee but shall not participate in the Investment Committee’s 
decision-making. They shall, however, be entitled to monitor 
compliance in relation to meeting notices, the materials submitted 
to the Investment Committee for decision-making, the investment 
decision-making procedures and other related matters.
Governing law: The Partnership Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the 
PRC.
Dispute resolution: Any dispute shall be submitted to the Beijing Arbitration 
Commission by the parties for arbitration in Beijing in accordance 
with the arbitration rules of the Commission.
The terms of the Partnership Agreement are determined after arm’s length negotiations 
among the parties.

[PDF PAGE 10]
10
III. REASONS AND BENEFITS FOR ENTERING INTO THE PARTNERSHIP 
AGREEMENT
The Fund has clearly defined investment scope and focuses on the nuclear technology 
application sector, including the production and preparation of isotopes, nuclear medical 
equipment and innovative drugs, industrial irradiation and inspection, security inspection 
and protection, as well as relevant applications of nuclear technology in the industrial, 
agricultural, medical, environmental protection and safety fields, together with key upstream 
and downstream links. The aforementioned investment directions are consistent with the 
Company’s existing business layout and its long-term strategic development direction. As 
a leading enterprise in the nuclear technology application field in China, the Company 
intends to leverage the investment deployment of the Fund across the niche segments of 
the nuclear technology application industry to create the synergistic effect of the “fund + 
industry” model. This will enable the Company to indirectly participate in the innovation 
and incubation of cutting-edge technologies, thereby reducing the cost of trial and error in 
independent research and development. Through the Fund, in addition to obtaining financial 
returns, the Company may secure preferential access to project cooperation rights, results 
commercialization rights and even strategic merger and acquisition opportunities, and rapidly 
transform external innovative achievements into new growth drivers for its own business. 
Leveraging the Fund’s industry events, project cooperation and other platforms, the Company 
may strengthen its exchanges and cooperation with peers and upstream and downstream 
enterprises along the industry chain, expand the scope for business cooperation, and empower 
its long-term development.
Pursuant to the currently applicable state-owned capital management system, if the Company 
makes direct investments, such investments would, in principle, be required to fall within 
the scope of the Company’s principal business. In addition, from the formation of an 
investment intention and project initiation through to the finalisation of the investment 
decision, the Company is required to undergo relatively complex internal decision-making 
and external approval procedures, with the overall process generally taking approximately 8 
to 12 months. Therefore, if the Company conducts investments primarily for the purpose of 
obtaining investment returns, the direct investment approach would entail relatively higher 
procedural and time costs. In contrast, through participation in the Fund, the Company’s 
investment capital is deployed by the Fund in a unified manner for project screening, 
investment decision-making and investment implementation, pursuant to the established 
investment strategy stipulated in the Partnership Agreement and under the decision-making 
and management mechanism of the meeting of the partners, the Investment Committee and 
the fund manager. Based on the past experience of similar funds, investments made through 
a fund generally take an average of approximately 3 to 4 months from project initiation to 
the completion of the investment decision. Accordingly, participation in the Fund helps to 
significantly reduce the procedural and time costs in the investment decision-making process 
and improve the efficiency of capital allocation and utilisation.

[PDF PAGE 11]
11
As to the risks in connection with the entering into the Partnership Agreement, the Company 
makes a relatively substantial investment in the Fund, with investment capital mainly to 
be recovered through exits from projects invested by the Fund; given the Fund’s four-year 
investment period and four-year exit period, with project exits concentrated in the latter part 
of the exit period, the Company’s investment may entail a lengthy capital recovery cycle, 
which may impair capital utilisation efficiency and give rise to the risk of long-term capital 
tie-up. In addition, the nuclear technology application sector features long research and 
development and commercialisation cycles, slow market cultivation and high susceptibility 
to policies and standards, and when compounded by technological iteration, cost volatility, 
insufficient capacity roll-out and mismatches between the Fund’s term and expected project 
exits, there exists a risk that investment returns may fall short of expectations.
In assessing the Partnership Agreement, the Directors have considered, among other things:
(a) the close alignment between the Fund’s exclusive focus on the nuclear technology 
application industry and the Group’s existing businesses and long-term development 
strategy;
(b) the potential financial returns and strategic benefits;
(c) the CNNC Fund’s accumulated extensive experience and project sourcing capabilities in 
the relevant industry;
(d) the benefits of obtaining diversified exposure to projects across different sub-sectors 
and stages of development through a professionally managed investment platform, as 
compared with the Group independently sourcing and managing a broad portfolio of 
minority investments;
(e) the investment restrictions, diversification measures, staged capital contribution 
mechanism, reporting arrangements and other investor protection mechanisms under the 
Partnership Agreement; and
(f) the risks associated with the investment.
The Directors have also considered the amount of the Company’s capital commitment 
relative to the Fund’s total committed capital, as well as the Group’s existing cash resources, 
liquidity position and anticipated capital expenditure requirements, and are of the view that 
the capital commitment will not have a material adverse impact on the Group’s operations 
or financial position. Having balanced the benefits and risks and made all reasonable 
enquiries, the Directors are of the view that the Company’s participation in the Fund 
represents a commercially reasonable means of obtaining financial and strategic exposure to 
investment opportunities in the nuclear technology application industry, and that the terms 
of the transaction are fair and reasonable and are in the interests of the Company and its 
shareholders as a whole.

[PDF PAGE 12]
12
IV. IMPLICATIONS OF THE LISTING RULES
As at the date of this announcement, CNNC directly and indirectly holds approximately 
73.83% of the Company’s total issued share capital through CIAE, NPIC, CNNC Fund and 
CNNC 404, and is the controlling Shareholder and a connected person of the Company. 
CNNC Capital and CNNC Fund are wholly-owned subsidiaries of CNNC. Therefore, CNNC 
Capital and CNNC Fund are associates of CNNC and constitute connected persons of the 
Company under Chapter 14A of the Listing Rules. Accordingly, the entering into of the 
Partnership Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereunder constitute connected 
transactions of the Company.
As one or more of the applicable percentage ratios of the transactions under the Partnership 
Agreement exceed 5% but are less than 25%, the transactions contemplated thereunder 
are subject to the reporting, announcement, annual review and independent shareholders’
approval requirements under Chapter 14A of the Listing Rules. The entering into of 
the Partnership Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereunder also constitute 
discloseable transactions of the Company.
V. EXTRAORDINARY GENERAL MEETING
The Company will convene an extraordinary general meeting for the Independent 
Shareholders to consider and approve, by way of ordinary resolution, the Partnership 
Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereunder. The Independent Board Committee 
of the Company will advise the Independent Shareholders on the Partnership Agreement 
and the transactions contemplated thereunder, and has appointed Rainbow Capital as 
the independent financial adviser to advise the Independent Board Committee and the 
Independent Shareholders on the Partnership Agreement and the transactions contemplated 
thereunder.
A circular, containing details of the Partnership Agreement and the transactions contemplated 
thereunder, the letter from the Independent Board Committee and advice from Rainbow 
Capital, will be despatched to the Shareholders within 15 working days after the date of this 
announcement.
The Directors (excluding the independent non-executive Directors, whose opinions will be 
formed after taking into account the advice of the independent financial adviser) consider that 
the terms of the Partnership Agreement have been determined after arm’s length negotiations 
on normal commercial terms, and that the transactions contemplated thereunder are fair and 
reasonable, will be entered into in the ordinary and usual course of business of the Group, 
and are in the interests of the Company and the Shareholders as a whole.

[PDF PAGE 13]
13
VI. GENERAL INFORMATION
The Company
Focusing on the two major industrial directions of nuclear healthcare and irradiation 
application, the Company is committed to providing integrated solutions for nuclear medicine 
and radiotherapy, as well as radiation technology promotion and application, forming a “6+N”
industrial layout with six major businesses as the core, including nuclides, nuclear medicines, 
nuclear medical equipment, integrated solutions for nuclear medicine, radioactive source and 
application, and irradiation application.
CNNC
China National Nuclear Corporation (中國核工業集團有限公司), a company established 
under the laws of the PRC on 29 June 1999, is the controlling shareholder of the Company. 
The ultimate beneficial owner of CNNC is the State-owned Assets Supervision and 
Administration Commission of the State Council.
CNNC Capital
CNNC Capital (formerly known as China National Nuclear Industry Construction 
Corporation Capital Holdings Limited (中國核工業建設集團資本控股有限公司)) was 
established in July 2016 with a registered capital of RMB7.38 billion. It is a wholly-owned 
subsidiary of China National Nuclear Corporation and a financial services and specialized 
capital operation platform. Its principal business activities include corporate management, 
management consulting, investment activities using proprietary funds, asset management 
services for investments made using proprietary funds and information consultancy services. 
CNNC Capital has developed a comprehensive industry-finance business cluster featuring 
synergies across investment, financial leasing, asset management, insurance and carbon asset 
management (投－租－理－險－碳), with business operations covering financial leasing, 
industrial funds, commercial factoring, insurance brokerage, captive insurance and carbon 
asset management. The ultimate beneficial owner of CNNC Capital is the State-owned Assets 
Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council.
CNNC Fund
CNNC Fund (formerly known as CNNC Industrial Fund Management (Beijing) Co., Ltd. (中
核產業基金管理(北京)有限公司)) was established on 4 July 2011 with a registered capital of 
RMB150 million. It is a wholly-owned subsidiary of CNNC Capital and is a licensed private 
equity fund management institution. Its principal business activities include non-securities 
investment management, consultancy and project investment, with a primary focus on equity 
investments across the upstream and downstream segments of the nuclear industry, including 
nuclear healthcare, nuclear technology applications and nuclear power. The ultimate 
beneficial owner of CNNC Fund is the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration 
Commission of the State Council.

[PDF PAGE 14]
14
As a private equity fund manager, CNNC Fund has long-term in-depth engagement in 
the nuclear technology application industry. As of 31 December 2025, CNNC Fund had 
successfully operated 8 funds, with the paid-in size of funds under management amounting 
to RMB4,823 million. In 2024, CNNC Fund received the “Excellent Management Team 
Award for State-owned Capital Funds” and the “Top 10 Excellent Investment Case Awards 
for State-owned Capital” from the Central SOE Investment Association; in 2024 and 2025, 
CNNC Fund was awarded the “Excellent Innovation Investment Case Award for State-owned 
Capital” by the Central SOE Investment Association for two consecutive years.
National Industrial Investment Fund
The National Industrial Investment Fund was established on 20 March 2025 with a registered 
capital of RMB59.6 billion. The National Industrial Investment Fund conducts equity 
investment, investment management and asset management business in the form of a private 
investment fund. There is no shareholder holding 30% or more of the equity interest in the 
National Industrial Investment Fund, and the single largest shareholder is the Ministry of 
Finance (holding approximately 21% of the shares).
Zhejiang Province Entrepreneurship Risk Investment Guide Fund
Zhejiang Province Entrepreneurship Risk Investment Guide Fund was established on 27 
February 2009, with a registered capital of RMB5 billion. Focusing on the development of 
Zhejiang Province’s “315” Scientific and Technological Innovation System, future industries 
and other priority sectors, the company invests in key technological innovation projects 
through cooperation with market-oriented institutions, with a particular focus on supporting 
early-stage and small enterprises, providing patient capital, and investing in hard technology, 
innovation platforms and innovative talent, thereby facilitating the commercialisation of 
scientific and technological achievements and fostering the development of new quality 
productive forces in light of local conditions. Its ultimate beneficial owner is Zhejiang 
Innovation Investment Group Co., Ltd. (浙江省創新投資集團有限公司), a state-owned 
enterprise in Zhejiang Province.

[PDF PAGE 15]
15
Jiaxing Changchuang Industrial Investment
Jiaxing Changchuang Industrial Investment was established on 9 April 2026 as an industrial 
chain fund with a target fund size of RMB3 billion established by the Jiaxing Municipal 
Finance Bureau. Focusing on Jiaxing’s “135N” advanced manufacturing clusters, the fund 
aims to accelerate the development of a modern industrial system and promote the extension, 
supplementation and strengthening of industrial chains. Jiaxing Changtou Venture Capital 
Co., Ltd. (嘉興長投創業投資有限公司) serves as the manager, executive partner and general 
partner of the fund. Its ultimate beneficial owner is Jiaxing Yangtze River Delta Innovation 
Investment Group Co., Ltd. (嘉興長三角創新投資集團有限公司), a state-owned enterprise 
based in Jiaxing.
Haiyan County State-owned Assets Investment
Haiyan County State-owned Assets Investment was established on 23 June 2015 with a 
registered capital of RMB10 million. Guided by the operating philosophy of “market￾orientation, specialisation and standardisation”, the company focuses on areas including 
industrial investment, capital operation, asset management and financial services, and is 
committed to supporting local industrial transformation and upgrading and the development 
of emerging industries through equity investments, fund cooperation and industrial guidance. 
Its ultimate beneficial owner is Haiyan County State-owned Industrial Investment Group Co., 
Ltd. (海鹽縣國有產業投資集團有限公司), a state-owned enterprise in Haiyan.

1. Based on the 2023 China Nuclear Medicine Industry Development Report, survey data 
on equipment upgrades in Class III-A hospitals, implementation documents for the “One 
County, One Department” plan issued by local health commissions, and research on the cost 
of establishing nuclear medicine departments in county-level hospitals, it is estimated that 
the total addressable market for intelligent nuclear medicine solutions in China from 2026 to 
2030 will amount to RMB5.518 billion, representing a CAGR of 35.2%.

[PDF PAGE 2]
2
2. Based on the “One County, One Department” policy, it is expected that 600 new nuclear 
medicine departments will be established nationwide during 2026 to 2030. Assuming a 
market share of 2.5%, 15 customers are expected to be secured, generating revenue of 
RMB106 million. The demand for intelligent upgrades among existing hospitals is expected 
to increase from 5% to 25%, with 52 customers contributing revenue of RMB24.61 million.
3. Leveraging the resources and channels of the Group, a closed-loop industrial chain can be 
formed. The sales team is expected to expand from 15 members in 2026 to 45 members by 
2030, covering 18 provinces, thereby ensuring its customer acquisition capability.
Forecast of cost of principal business
The forecast of the cost of the principal business of the Nuclear Medicine Development Center 
adopted in this valuation is set out below:

The above forecast primarily takes into account the impact of revenue expansion on gross profit 
margin, the impact on costs arising from the factors described under the section headed “Forecast 
of Revenue from Principal Business”, and the results of discussions with the management.
Forecast of capital expenditure
As the Nuclear Medicine Development Center held 7 intellectual properties involving co-owners as 
at the Valuation Benchmark Date, and considering that the forecasts are based on full ownership, 
it is expected that RMB1.5 million will be payable to purchase the 50% interest in the intangible 
assets held by Peking Union Medical College Hospital through simulated acquisition of the other 
party’s equity.
Other parameters used in the revenue forecast
The following parameters were also adopted in preparing the revenue forecast of the Nuclear 
Medicine Development Center:
Urban maintenance and construction tax rate 7% of the value-added tax payable
Education surcharge tax rate 5% of the value-added tax payable
Enterprise income tax rate 25%

[PDF PAGE 3]
3
Discount Rate
Discount rate model
Under the principle that the earnings metric shall be the same as that for discount rate, the earnings 
metric adopted in this valuation is free cash flow to the firm, the discount rate is determined based 
on the weighted average cost of capital (WACC). The WACC model is expressed by the following 
mathematical formula:
WACC = Rd × (1 – T) ×
D
+ Re×
E
D + E D + E
Where: Re
: expected rate of return on equity;
Rd
: expected rate of return on debt;
E: value of net assets;
D: value of debt;
T: income tax rate.
Determination of cost of equity capital
In determining the cost of equity capital, the Independent Valuer adopted the Capital Asset Pricing 
Model (“CAPM”). The CAPM is a widely applied method for estimating investor returns and the 
cost of equity capital. The CAPM can be expressed by the following mathematical formula:
Re = Rf + ERP × β + ε
Where: Rf
: risk-free interest rate;
ERP: equity risk premium;
β: systematic risk coefficient of equity;
ε: enterprise’s specific risk adjustment coefficient.

[PDF PAGE 4]
4
Valuation process of specific parameters
1. Selection of comparable companies
The comparable companies were selected with reference to the following criteria:
(1) The stocks of comparable listed companies have been listed for not less than 24 months 
and are actively traded;
(2) The comparable listed companies are in the same industry as the appraised entity or 
affected by the same economic policies;
(3) The comparable listed companies’ principal activities are identical to those of the 
appraised entity, with the revenue from the identical principal activities constituting no 
less than 50% of the total revenue;
(4) The comparable listed companies exhibit similarity to the appraised entity in terms of 
asset scale, profitability, growth potential and stage of development.
Based on the above selection criteria, the Independent Valuer selected the following listed 
companies as comparable listed companies:
No. Stock Code Company Name
1 000948.SZ Nantian Information
2 002230.SZ iFLYTEK
3 002368.SZ Taiji Computer
4 300300.SZ Strait Innovation
5 300550.SZ Heren Health
6 002261.SZ Talkweb Information
7 002777.SZ Jiuyuan Yinhai
Risk-free return rate (Rf
)
The yield of treasury bonds is usually considered risk-free because the risk of holding such bonds 
that cannot be repaid at maturity is so insignificant that it can be ignored. The Independent Valuer 
determined the risk-free return rate by querying the average yield to maturity of treasury bonds 
traded near the Valuation Benchmark Date with over ten years remaining to maturity through 
iFinD Information, arriving at Rf
 of 2.21%.

[PDF PAGE 5]
5
Determination of equity risk premium (ERP)
Equity risk premium is the expected excess return that an investor would request on an equity 
investment with risk that is the same as the overall market average risk, i.e., the compensation 
for risk over the risk-free interest rate. Investment return in the equity market is a typical 
representation of return in the capital market. Risk-return in the equity market is the excess over 
the risk-free return rate that an investor expects from investing in the equity market and can also 
be considered a typical representation of equity risk premium.
The Independent Valuer estimates the investment return (Rm) and equity risk premium (ERP) 
(Rm-Rf
) of the equity market in China as follows:
(1) Selection of index for measuring investment yield
The CSI 300 Index is an index covering both the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock markets, 
reflecting the comprehensive changes in the stock prices of representative stocks with strong 
liquidity and large scale. The constituent stocks of the index can more truly reflect the 
returns of mainstream investment in the market. Therefore, the CSI 300 Index was selected to 
estimate the investment yield of the PRC stock market.
(2) The 10-year period is selected as the time span for the calculation of investment yield. For 
each constituent stock of CSI 300, the investment yield for the past ten years is calculated 
to minimize the impact of non-systematic stock volatility. The term used to calculate the 
investment yield for 2025 is from 2015 to 2024, and the investment yield for subsequent 
years is calculated similarly.
(3) Calculation of annual investment yield (Rm)
Two calculation methods are adopted: arithmetic mean and geometric mean. Based on 
comparative analysis, the Independent Valuer believes the geometric mean can better reflect 
the growth of the yield rate, and therefore the geometric mean is used as the calculation of 
final annual investment yield (Rm).
(4) Determination of equity risk premium (ERP) (Rm – Rf
)
The Independent Valuer selected the yield to maturity of treasury bonds with a remaining 
maturity of more than 10 years at the end of each year as the risk-free interest rate Rf. After 
the above steps, the Independent Valuer estimated the ERP for 2024 to be 6.35%.
Determination of the risk coefficient β of comparable companies relative to the stock market
A correlation t test was performed on β coefficient of the above comparable listed companies.

[PDF PAGE 6]
6
Calculation of β coefficient without financial leverage of comparable companies
For the β coefficient with financial leverage (βL) available for these comparable listed companies, 
the Independent Valuer has unlevered it to the β coefficient without financial leverage (βU) 
according to the capital structure of the corresponding listed companies. The calculation process is 
as follows:

Calculation of β coefficient with target capital structure of the appraised entity
It is calculated based on the average value of the β coefficients without financial leverage of 
comparable companies and the target capital structure, the calculation formula is as follows:
βL = (1 + (1 − T) × D/E) × βU
Where: βL is β coefficient with the target capital structure of the appraised entity
βU is the average value of β coefficient without financial leverage of comparable 
companies
D/E is the target capital structure, which in this instance is taken as the average capital 
structure of comparable companies.
Blume adjustment of β coefficient
The β coefficient of comparable listed companies estimated by the Independent Valuer based on 
historical data represents the historical β coefficient. The discount rate is used in discounting the 
future expected income, so the discount rate to be estimated is also the expected discount rate 
in the future. As a result, it is required to estimate the expected β coefficient in the future. The 
Independent Valuer adopted the Blume Adjustment method to adjust the β coefficient estimated 
based on historical data.

[PDF PAGE 7]
7
In practice, the adjustment concept and method proposed by Blume are as follows:
a = 0.35 + 0.65βL
Where: a is the adjusted β
βL is the estimated historical β.
The adjusted risk coefficient β of the appraised entity is 1.0729.
Determination of specific risk return (ε)
The specific risk return (ε) is the return on non-systematic risk arising from the specific factors 
of the appraised entity. A reasonable specific risk return (ε) is determined by adopting the 
comprehensive analysis method in the valuation, namely, after comprehensively considering the 
relevant factors, such as the asset scale, operation stage, market competition, reliance on key 
customers and suppliers, corporate governance and capital structure of the appraised entity. The 
adjusted specific risk coefficient adopted in this valuation was 3%.
Calculation of cost of equity capital
Substituting the relevant data into the Re formula:
Re = Rf + β × (R m − Rf) + ε
yields the cost of equity capital as 12.02%.
Determination of cost of debt capital
The one-year Loan Prime Rate (“LPR”) of banks was adopted as the cost of debt capital, i.e.,

Calculation of WACC

Valuation result
As disclosed in the Announcement, as of 30 September 2025, the Nuclear Medicine Development 
Center of CIRC had current assets of RMB83,500, non-current assets of RMB5.7274 million and 
current liabilities of RMB1.5412 million, resulting in a book value of net assets of RMB4.2697 
million. According to the Asset Valuation Report, the appraised value of the Nuclear Medicine 
Development Center as at the Valuation Benchmark Date was RMB18.40 million, representing an 
appraisal surplus of RMB14.13 million and an appreciation of approximately 330.9% over its book 
value. The aforesaid difference was primarily attributable to the fact that the valuation under the 
income approach not only took into account the value of all tangible assets, intangible assets and 
liabilities recognised in the balance sheet of the appraised entity, but also considered the appraised 
entity’s resource integration capability and overall earning capacity, which were not reflected in its

ENTERING INTO THE SHAREHOLDERS’ AGREEMENT
On 28 July 2026, the Company entered into the Shareholders’ Agreement with CNNC Zhejiang 
Science and Technology Innovation, in respect of the establishment of the joint venture company, 
CNNC Fuzhi. Pursuant to the Shareholders’ Agreement, the registered capital of CNNC Fuzhi 
is RMB50 million, among which, RMB45 million will be contributed by the Company by way 
of a combination of non-monetary assets and cash, comprising RMB26.60 million in cash and 
RMB18.40 million in the form of the net assets of the Nuclear Medicine Development Center; 
and RMB5 million will be contributed by CNNC Zhejiang Science and Technology Innovation 
in cash. Upon the establishment of CNNC Fuzhi, the Company and CNNC Zhejiang Science and 
Technology Innovation will hold 90% and 10% equity interests in CNNC Fuzhi, respectively, 
and CNNC Fuzhi will become a non-wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company.
IMPLICATIONS OF THE LISTING RULES
As at the date of this announcement, CNNC directly and indirectly holds approximately 73.83% 
of the Company’s total issued share capital through CIAE, NPIC, CNNC Fund and 404 Company, 
and is the controlling Shareholder and connected person of the Company. CNNC Capital is a 
wholly-owned subsidiary of CNNC, CNNC Science and Technology Innovation is a wholly￾owned subsidiary of CNNC Capital, and CNNC Zhejiang Science and Technology Innovation is 
a non-wholly-owned subsidiary of CNNC Science and Technology Innovation. Therefore, CNNC 
Zhejiang Science and Technology Innovation is an associate of CNNC and a connected person 
of the Company under Chapter 14A of the Listing Rules. The entering into the Shareholders’
Agreement and the transaction contemplated thereunder thus constitute a connected transaction 
of the Company.
As the highest applicable percentage ratio calculated under the Listing Rules in respect of 
the transaction under the Shareholders’ Agreement exceeds 0.1% but is less than 5%, such 
transaction is only subject to the reporting and announcement requirements but exempt from 
independent Shareholders’ approval requirement under Chapter 14A of the Listing Rules.

[PDF PAGE 2]
2
INTRODUCTION
On 28 July 2026, the Company entered into the Shareholders’ Agreement with CNNC Zhejiang 
Science and Technology Innovation, in respect of the establishment of the joint venture company, 
CNNC Fuzhi. Pursuant to the Shareholders’ Agreement, the registered capital of CNNC Fuzhi 
is RMB50 million, among which, RMB45 million will be contributed by the Company by way 
of a combination of non-monetary assets and cash, comprising RMB26.60 million in cash and 
RMB18.40 million in the form of the net assets of the Nuclear Medicine Development Center; 
and RMB5 million will be contributed by CNNC Zhejiang Science and Technology Innovation 
in cash. Upon the establishment of CNNC Fuzhi, the Company and CNNC Zhejiang Science and 
Technology Innovation will hold 90% and 10% equity interests in CNNC Fuzhi, respectively, and 
CNNC Fuzhi will become a non-wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company.

Upon the establishment of CNNC Fuzhi, each contributing party shall

Valuation method 
of the contributed 
assets and basis of 
consideration:
This valuation is conducted on the net assets of the Nuclear Medicine 
Development Center, which the Company intends to contribute as 
non-monetary capital, and the valuation results under the income approach 
are adopted as the final valuation conclusion. According to the Asset 
Valuation Report issued by the Independent Valuer, as of the Valuation 
Reference Date (30 September 2025), the carrying amount of the net 
assets of the Nuclear Medicine Development Center is RMB4.2697 
million, the valuation value is RMB18.40 million, and the valuation 
appreciation amounts to RMB14.1303 million (with an appreciation rate 
of 330.95%).
A summary of the key contents of the Asset Valuation Report is set out in 
the section headed “Valuation of the Net Assets of the Nuclear Medicine 
Development Center” of this announcement.
The consideration was determined after arm’s length negotiations between 
the Company and CNNC Zhejiang Science and Technology Innovation, 
taking into account, among other things, the valuation conclusions set out 
in the Asset Valuation Report issued by the Independent Valuer.
Business scope: General items: software development, software sales, big data center 
construction, data sales; technical services, technical development, 
consulting services, technical exchange, technology transfer, and 
technology promotion; research and development, sales, and operation 
and maintenance services of equipment and systems; commercialization 
of scientific and technological achievements; sales of radiation protection 
and monitoring equipment; sales of electronic products; maintenance 
of electronic and mechanical equipment (excluding special equipment); 
import and export of goods; import and export of technology; and 
conference and exhibition services (except for items subject to approval 
by law, the business activities shall be conducted independently with the 
business licences in accordance with the laws).
Licensed items: sales of pharmaceuticals; sales of Class II and Class 
III medical devices; sales of Class II and Class III radiation equipment 
(subject to the approval by the industry and commerce authorities).

[PDF PAGE 4]
4
Management 
organization and 
legal representative 
of CNNC Fuzhi:
CNNC Fuzhi shall have a shareholders’ general meeting composed of 
all shareholders which acts as the organ of authority of CNNC Fuzhi 
and exercises its functions and powers in accordance with the Company 
Law and relevant laws, administrative regulations and the articles of 
association.
CNNC Fuzhi shall not establish a board of directors, but shall have one 
director who manages the company’s affairs. Such director shall exercise 
the powers and functions of the board of directors as prescribed under 
the Company Law. The director shall be recommended by China Isotope 
and elected by the shareholders’ general meeting, and shall serve as the 
legal representative of the company. The director shall be responsible 
to the shareholders’ general meeting and shall exercise the powers and 
functions as stipulated in the articles of association or as delegated by the 
shareholders’ general meeting. The term of office of the director shall be 
three years, and the director may be re-elected upon expiration of such 
term.
CNNC Fuzhi shall have a general manager, who shall be recommended 
by China Isotope and shall be responsible to the director managing the 
company’s affairs, and shall bear overall responsibility for the daily 
production and operation management of the company. It shall have three 
other senior management personnel, all of whom shall be recommended 
by China Isotope. The specific working mechanism shall be determined by 
the articles of association of CNNC Fuzhi. The appointment or dismissal 
of senior management personnel shall be decided by the director.
Equity transfer and 
pledge:
In the event that a shareholder desires to transfer all or any part of its 
equity interests in CNNC Fuzhi, a written notice with respect to such 
equity transfer shall be given to the other shareholders.
Under the same conditions, the other shareholders of CNNC Fuzhi have a 
right of first refusal. The other shareholders, as the preferred transferees, 
shall respond within thirty days after the transferor gives a written notice 
of its transfer request; otherwise, the transferor shall have the right to 
transfer such equity interests to any party other than the shareholders.
When a shareholder of CNNC Fuzhi transfers all or part of its equity 
interests to any party other than the other shareholders, the transferor shall 
submit to the other shareholders of CNNC Fuzhi a copy of the written 
agreement executed with the transferee, setting forth the corresponding 
rights and obligations under such transfer.
Specifically, if the Company or CNNC Zhejiang Science and Technology 
Innovation transfers its equity in CNNC Fuzhi to a subsidiary it controls, 
no consent from the other shareholders of CNNC Fuzhi will be required, 
and those other shareholders of CNNC Fuzhi shall be deemed to have 
waived their right of first refusal.
Any equity transfer of CNNC Fuzhi shall not impede the operations of 
CNNC Fuzhi or affect its organizational structure. After the transfer is 
approved, CNNC Fuzhi shall file for the change of registration with the 
market regulation authority within 15 days.

[PDF PAGE 5]
5
Valuation of the Net Assets of the Nuclear Medicine Development Center
The summary of the Asset Valuation Report issued by the Independent Valuer is set out below:
Valuation Purpose
China Isotope & Radiation Corporation plans to make an outbound capital contribution, for which 
the market value of the net assets of the China Isotope & Radiation Corporation Nuclear Medicine 
Development Center as at the Benchmark Date needs to be assessed, so as to provide a reference 
basis for the aforesaid economic activity.
Valuation Object and Scope
The valuation object is the net asset value of the China Isotope & Radiation Corporation Nuclear 
Medicine Development Center; the valuation scope covers all assets and related liabilities reported 
as of 30 September 2025, specifically including: current assets of RMB83,500, non-current assets 
of RMB5,727,400, and current liabilities of RMB1,541,200.
Valuation Benchmark Date
The Benchmark Date for asset appraisal is 30 September 2025.
Valuation Methods
Selection of the Income Approach Result
The basic methods of enterprise value valuation mainly include the income approach, market 
approach and asset-based approach.
The appraised entity operates on a going concern basis. The selection of economic and technical 
parameters used in the asset-based approach is supported by sufficient data as a foundation and 
basis, and the financial data have been audited. There are no off-book assets that would have a 
material impact on the value of the valuation object and that are difficult to identify and assess; 
therefore, the asset-based approach can be applied.
The income approach evaluates assets from the perspective of expected profitability, which 
can fully reflect the overall value of an enterprise. The appraised entity is an enterprise with a 
certain level of profitability. Considering the relatively stable historical annual performance of 
the appraised entity, its future earnings can be reasonably projected and measured in monetary 
terms, the income period can be reasonably determined, and the risks associated with obtaining the 
expected future earnings can be measured. Therefore, the income approach has been selected for 
this valuation.
A prerequisite for applying the market approach is that comparable reference entities have an 
open market with active trading, as well as the necessary information regarding such transactions 
is accessible. Currently, among domestic listed companies in the same industry as the appraised 
entity, few are comparable in terms of business structure, operating model, enterprise scale, 
asset allocation, and future growth potential. In addition, there have been few comparable equity 
transactions in the property rights trading market involving entities similar to the appraised entity 
recently. Information such as the relevant transaction background and the operating and financial 
data of the transaction cases cannot be obtained through public channels, and thus the basic 
conditions for applying the market approach are not met.

[PDF PAGE 6]
6
The asset-based approach considers the re-acquisition channels of assets and reflects the 
replacement value of an enterprise’s existing assets. The income approach evaluates profitability 
from the perspective of the enterprise’s future earning capacity. The asset-based approach only 
reasonably determines the market value of the assets as at the Benchmark Date from a static 
perspective. In applying the income approach, consideration is given not only to the value of all 
tangible assets, intangible assets, and liabilities already reflected on the enterprise’s balance sheet, 
but also to the enterprise’s capital capacity, the integrated resource capability of all its assets, its 
comprehensive profitability, and its production capacity, which are not shown on the balance sheet 
of the appraised entity.
Based on the purpose of this valuation, in conjunction with the valuation object and the applicable 
type of value, and following comparative analysis, it is considered that the conclusion derived from 
the income approach can more comprehensively and reasonably reflect the net asset value of the 
appraised entity as at the Benchmark Date. In summary, the result of the income approach has been 
selected as the conclusion for this valuation.
Valuation Input Data
Valuation Model and Key Parameters:
The income approach adopted in this valuation is the discounted cash flow method, using 
free cash flow to the firm as the cash flow metric. The net asset value is derived indirectly 
through the valuation of the overall enterprise value.
The calculation model is as follows:
Net asset value = overall enterprise value – interest-bearing debt value
(1) Overall enterprise value
Overall enterprise value refers to the sum of net asset value and the value of interest￾bearing debt. According to the allocation and use of the assets of the appraised entity, 
the overall enterprise value is calculated according to the following formula:
Overall enterprise value = value of operating assets + value of surplus assets + value of 
non-operating assets – value of non-operating liabilities

[PDF PAGE 7]
7
i. Value of operating assets
Value of operating assets is calculated as follows:
P=
n
Fi +
Fn+1 ∑ (1+r)i r×(1+r)n
i=1
Where:
P: the value of the enterprise’s operating assets as at the Valuation Benchmark 
Date;
Fi: the expected free cash flow of the enterprise in year i after the Valuation 
Benchmark Date;
Fn+1: the expected free cash flow of the enterprise in the last year of the detailed 
forecast period;
r: Discount rate (in this case the weighted average cost of capital, WACC);
n: Detailed forecast period;
i: Year i of the detailed forecast period (mid-year discounting).
a) Income period
Through analysis of the development prospects of the industry in which 
the appraised entity operates and the entity’s own operating conditions, no 
matters that could affect the entity’s going concern have been identified. For 
this valuation, it is assumed that the appraised entity will continue as a going 
concern after the Valuation Benchmark Date, and the income period is set as 
a perpetual period.
b) Income indicator
In accordance with the principle that the expected income metric and the 
discount rate are consistent in scope, the enterprise value income indicator 
for the valuation object is determined using free cash flow to the firm.
Free cash flow to the firm = net profit before interest and after tax + 
depreciation and amortization – capital expenditure – net increase in working 
capital

[PDF PAGE 8]
8
c) Discount rate
The earnings metric adopted in this valuation is free cash flow to the firm, 
the discount rate is determined based on the weighted average cost of capital 
model (WACC) under the principle that the earnings metric shall be the same 
as that for discount rate. The calculation formula of which is as follows:
WACC= Ke ×
E
+ Kd×(1-t) ×
D
E+D E+D
Where:
Ke: Cost of equity capital;
Kd: Cost of interest-bearing debt capital;
E: market value of equity;
D: market value of interest-bearing debt;
t: income tax rate.
Of which, the cost of equity capital is calculated using the Capital Asset 
Pricing Model (CAPM). The calculation formula is as follows:
Ke= Rf + MRP × βL + Rc
Where:
Rf: risk-free rate of return;
MRP: market risk premium;
βL: systematic risk factor for equity;
Rc: Enterprise-specific risk adjustment factor.

[PDF PAGE 9]
9
ii. Value of surplus assets
Surplus assets refer to assets that exceed the needs of the production and operation 
of the enterprise as at the Valuation Benchmark Date and are not covered in the 
forecast of free cash flow to the firm after the Valuation Benchmark Date. The 
surplus assets of the appraised entity have been valued using the cost approach in 
this valuation.
iii. Value of non-operating assets and liabilities
Non-operating assets and liabilities refer to assets and liabilities that are unrelated 
to the operations of the appraised entity and are not covered in the forecast of free 
cash flow to the firm after the Valuation Benchmark Date. The cost approach has 
been adopted in this valuation.
(2) Value of interest-bearing debt
Interest-bearing debt refers to debts of the appraised entity that bear interest as at the 
Valuation Benchmark Date. The appraised entity had no interest-bearing debt as at the 
Valuation Benchmark Date.
Principal Assumptions Underlying the Valuation
Basic Assumptions
1. In the open market assumption, it is assumed that for assets to be traded or intended to be 
traded in the market, the parties to the asset transaction shall have equal status, and also have 
opportunity and time to gain sufficient market information, so as to make rational judgement 
on functions, purpose and trading prices of assets;
2. In the transaction assumption, it is assumed that all assets to be valued are in the process of 
transaction, and the Independent Valuer makes estimation in a simulated market according 
to the transaction conditions of assets to be valued. The transaction assumption is one of the 
most basic prerequisites that asset valuation can be carried out;
3. In the going concern assumption, it is assumed that the appraised entity, based on the existing 
assets and resources, will not stop business for various reasons in the foreseeable future, but 
will continue to operate legally.

[PDF PAGE 10]
10
General Assumptions
1. It is assumed that there are no significant changes in the current relevant laws, regulations, 
policies, and macroeconomic situation of the country, and that there are no significant 
changes in the political, economic, and social environment of the regions where the parties to 
the transactions are located;
2. It is assumed that the industry in which the appraised entity operates maintains a stable 
development trend, with no significant changes in industry policies, management systems, 
and relevant regulations;
3. It is assumed that there are no significant changes in interest rates, exchange rates, tax 
benchmarks and rates, policy-related collection fees, etc. related to the appraised entity after 
the Valuation Benchmark Date;
4. It is assumed that no force majeure or unforeseeable factors have a significant adverse impact 
on the appraised entity after the Valuation Benchmark Date.
Special Assumptions
1. It is assumed that the general information relating to the business operation, property rights 
documentation, policy documents and other relevant materials provided by the client and the 
appraised entity are true and valid;
2. It is assumed that the purchase, acquisition and construction of the assets involved in the 
valuation object are in accordance with the relevant laws and regulations of the PRC;
3. It is assumed that the physical assets involved in the valuation object have no major technical 
failures that affect their continuous use, and that their key components and materials have no 
potential significant quality defects;
4. It is assumed that the assets within the scope of the appraisal are genuine and complete, free 
from title defects, not involved in any mortgage, lien, or guarantee matters, and not subject to 
any other transaction restrictions;
5. It is assumed that the management of the appraised entity is responsible, stable, and capable 
of discharging its duties after the Valuation Benchmark Date;
6. It is assumed that the appraised entity, based on its existing management methods and 
levels, maintains the same business scope and methods as it currently has after the Valuation 
Benchmark Date;
7. All licenses, permits, consents, or other legal or administrative authorizations issued by 
relevant local and national government authorities and institutions required for the asset 
usage methods underlying the value estimates in this valuation report are assumed to be valid, 
compliant, and in normal use as of the Valuation Benchmark Date, and it is assumed that 
such documents can be renewed or reissued upon expiration;

[PDF PAGE 11]
11
8. It is assumed that the relevant data of listed companies sourced from iFinD Information are 
authentic and reliable;
9. During the forecast period, the core management and technical personnel of the appraised 
entity are relatively stable, and no significant changes affecting business development and 
profit realization will occur;
10. It is assumed that the cash inflow of the appraised entity after the Valuation Benchmark Date 
is even, and the cash outflow is likewise even.
Valuation Conclusion
Based on the Asset Valuation Report, having performed the aforesaid asset valuation procedures 
and adopted the aforesaid appraisal methodologies, the Independent Valuer determined that the 
appraised value of the Nuclear Medicine Development Center as at the Valuation Benchmark Date 
was RMB18.40 million.
INFORMATION ON THE NUCLEAR MEDICINE DEVELOPMENT CENTER
Principal Business Activities
The Nuclear Medicine Development Center was established in June 2022 as an internal business 
unit of China Isotope & Radiation Corporation. Its principal business is to incubate the intelligent 
nuclear medicine industry. It has successfully developed the intelligent nuclear medicine 
information system and achieved its commercialization.

REASONS FOR AND BENEFITS OF ENTERING INTO THE SHAREHOLDERS’
AGREEMENT TO ESTABLISH CNNC FUZHI
CNNC Fuzhi will undertake the business of the Nuclear Medicine Development Center and focus 
on the intelligent nuclear medicine industry, and will integrate the entire industrial chain “nuclear 
medicine”, and establish a synergistic development model combining “intelligent nuclear medicine, 
pharmaceuticals, and equipment”. This will drive the transformation of the business model from 
“single-product supply” to “full-value-chain integrated services”, leading the standardization 
and intelligent transformation of the nuclear medicine industry. It will continuously improve the 
full-chain ecosystem, consolidate its industry-leading position, and cultivate new profit growth 
drivers for the Company. 
FINANCIAL IMPACT OF THE TRANSACTION
The Group anticipates an unaudited pre-tax gain, net of transaction costs and expenses, of 
approximately RMB0 arising from the Company’s capital contribution in the form of the net assets
